_capture.note: A statement this script runs, sorting twice: a window function’s sort and an ORDER BY … LIMIT the planner turns into a top-k. It exists because the estate’s widest plan carries no SORT_ORDER, and a promised key with no captured value is the hole 33ih came out of. Node counts here are NOT the counts the API returned.
_capture.trimRule: every distinct tag kept, then filled to 60 nodes in original order; edges filtered to kept nodes on from_id/to_id; stage_data to one entry; of the node arrays metrics and expressions, the 18 metrics the parser reads by label are kept and the rest capped to 1 entries; meta_data keeps every key, and values of keys the parser does not read are capped at 120 characters
_capture.statement:
WITH ranked AS (
      SELECT statement_id, statement_type, total_duration_ms,
             row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY statement_type ORDER BY total_duration_ms DESC) AS rank
      FROM system.query.history
      WHERE start_time >= current_timestamp() - INTERVAL 2 DAYS
    )
    SELECT statement_type, count(*) AS runs, sum(total_duration_ms) AS ms
    FROM ranked WHERE rank <= 100
    GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY ms DESC LIMIT 20
